newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to sell 5-10 pct of CANTV in local mkts.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to sell 5-10 pct of CANTV in local mkts.

text.p: The Venezuelan government plans to place between five and 10 percent of CANTV on the domestic capital markets as part of a global offering of its minority stake of the telephone company, a top government official said Friday.
The government expects to raise $1 billion from the sale of part of its 49 percent stake in the company in November, Leon added.

"The economic cabinet approved that...between five and 10 percentage points of the company will be offered locally," Armando Leon, vice planning minister, told reporters. "The placement will not be done on just one day."
The government has said that about nine percent of the company will be offered to employees.
U.S. investment banks Lehman Brothers and SBC Warburg are co-managers of the global issue.
Local brokerages Merinvest and Valores Santander - a unit of Spain's Banco Santander - are managing the placement of shares on the Venezuelan market.
The government sold part of CANTV in 1991, when VenWorld, a consortium led by GTE Corp, bought a 40 percent stake and employees bought 11 percent of the company.

In addition to GTE Corp with a 51 percent stake, VenWorld is owned by Electricidad de Caracas with 16 percent, Telefonica de Espana SA with 16 percent, Venezuela's Banco Mercantil BM.CR with 12 percent and AT&T Corp with five percent.
